comments.author: Arlen
comments.body: One thing to note is that the permits gotten by doing royal commands are listed in the order you need to get them. In effect, each one is a prerequisite for the next. Also note that you get the Oceania permit when your nations leader tells you about the circumnavigation event, as opposed to when you complete it. The East Coast of Latin America quests comes from your nations leader. Southeast Asia quests come from your nation's consul in India (at the harbor). I'm not sure when you get told about the circumnavigation, but as I said the permit comes from your nations leader. The West Coast of Latin America quests can be gotten from your consul in Rio de Janiero. Then you will need to discover Panama by visiting it (actually going into the city, not just docking). According to Elroyy you also need to discover Portobelo, but that's not hard at all. The Panama Canal quests can be gotten in Santiego from your consul again. Then before you can get the Suez quest, you need to discover Suez, and possibly Cairo. The Suez quests come from your nation's leader (venicians have it easy). After that, it will probably be East Asia, and the consuls are in Manilla I believe. As of February 9, 2012, that is the last known port permit. Happy Sailing!

comments.author: Cornelia
comments.body:
If you have SEA then your next permit is Oceania (Australia/New Zealand). You have to start the circumnav to get it, but only the first dialog at your palace. You do not have to complete it yet, you get the permit just for clicking the button.

If you want to hold off on circumnavigation, you'll probably run into the next dialog when trying to report discos in Seville palace. It's OK, click through the dialog, then just ignore the old man outside when you leave. He'll still be there whenever you feel like doing the quest.

Once you have the Oceania permit, the West SA IQs should show up.
